text:
dev-anna: quick check — hitting an edge case in /v1/complete routing. client sends model_id="redwood-llama-70b" + region_hint="eu-west-1" and there is no matching dedicated capacity so runtime falls back to a quantized variant (redwood-llama-70b-quant). response today looks like:
```
{
  "model": "redwood-llama-70b-quant",
  "model_version": "v2",
  "choices": [...]
}
```
clients sometimes compare the echoed "model" to their requested model_id and treat this as a failure. question: do we want to guarantee an explicit served_model object with structured fields so clients can tell "this was a family-compatible fallback" vs "client requested variant was served"? also: backward compat — a lot of older clients expect a top-level string "model". thoughts?

sam-engineer: +1 on an explicit object. minimal fields: id, family, variant (optional), reason. e.g. served_model: { id: "redwood-llama-70b-quant", family: "redwood-llama-70b", variant: "quant", reason: "fallback-region-capacity" } :thumbsup:

mike-plat: agree. also we need to record which routing hint actually influenced the choice (region vs tier vs allow_fallback). maybe served_model.reason could be normalized enum values: "pinned", "fallback_capacity", "region_routing". and include served_model.hint_trigger: "region_hint" if that's what caused it.

jess-reviewer: code-review ping — PR draft in my fork https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321 updates the response shape to include served_model. important: we should not break parsers. propose we keep the current top-level "model" string for at least one release, and add served_model object. then mark "model" deprecated in API docs.

dev-anna: that sounds right. proposal: add served_model object (id, family, variant, reason, hint_trigger) in all responses, and keep "model" for a deprecation window (3 months). clients can migrate by inspecting served_model.family vs requested model_id. i'll open a PR to the API contract doc and the runtime change.

sam-engineer: small perf note — served_model should be tiny; avoid embedding large compatibility metadata. if we need detailed inference lineage we can add an opt-in "served_model.debug" that is only present when debug=true.

mike-plat: question: what about the model selection param semantics? currently model_id is used as a preference, but if allow_fallback=false we must fail rather than return a variant. do we have that param? i remember routing had model_selection_policy and allow_fallback was in the client SDKs but not enforced server-side. we should make server-side behavior explicit in the contract.

jess-reviewer: yes — we should add a required boolean query param/field: "allow_fallback" (default true for backwards compat). if false and exact model not available return 409 with structured error code "model_unavailable_exact". that keeps things clear.

dev-anna: agreed. summary of action items:
- add served_model object in all /v1/complete responses (small shape) and keep legacy "model" string for deprecation window
- add allow_fallback boolean (default true) to the API contract; if false, return 409 + error code when exact model_id cannot be served
- route hint metadata: include served_model.hint_trigger enum for region/tier/pinned/fallback
- add opt-in debug field for full routing trace behind debug=true

jess-reviewer: i'll update the PR and add a changelog entry + SDK notes. pinging @mike-plat for API sign-off.

ci-bot: Deploy bot: noted PR reference 4321 — please add integration test verifying both legacy "model" string is returned and new "served_model" object present.

mike-plat: API sign-off with one request: add an explicit compatibility note that "family compatibility" is defined by semantic model_family matching and supported quantized/compacted variants are considered compatible. i'll write a short spec fragment. :white_check_mark:

dev-anna: great — i'll open the runtime PR tomorrow and link to jess's contract PR. assigning follow-ups: @jess-reviewer (contract + changelog), @sam-engineer (client SDK updates), @mike-plat (compatibility spec). thanks all.

sam-engineer: sounds good. i'll add a smoke test to the SDKs that asserts served_model.family exists when a fallback happened.

dev-anna: final note — for telemetry, let's tag logs with served_model.family and hint_trigger so we can track how often fallbacks happen by region. i'll add to the observability ticket. :eyes:
